title: Field Service Software With QuickBooks Integration (2026)
description: Which field service apps sync with QuickBooks Online or Desktop, from which plan, and one-way or two-way: Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceM8, Kickserv and more.
h1: Field service software with QuickBooks integration: plans, versions and what syncs
body:
If your books already live in QuickBooks, the field service app you pick decides how much retyping you do every week. The questions that matter are simple: does it work with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop or both, which plan do you need before the sync turns on, and does data flow one way or both ways? This guide answers those for eight tools, using only each vendor's pricing page and its own QuickBooks help page, all checked on 2026-11-22. Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. QuickBooks itself is a separate Intuit subscription and isn't included in any of these prices.

Checked 2026-11-22.

The eight tools, QuickBooks first

  • Jobber: QuickBooks Online only, from Connect. Core ($29/mo billed annually) has no QuickBooks sync; it starts on Connect. Jobber's help center says its new integration syncs clients, products and services, invoices, payments (including Jobber Payments payouts, tips and refunds) and timesheets one way from Jobber to QuickBooks, automatically. Jobber is the source of truth, so edits belong in Jobber, and "paid" status on invoices doesn't sync back. Supported versions are QuickBooks Online Simple Start, Essentials, Plus and Advanced in the US. Jobber doesn't sync to QuickBooks Desktop; Desktop clients can only be imported from a CSV once. The new integration is being rolled out gradually, so some accounts still run Jobber's older (legacy) integration. More: Jobber pricing.
  • Housecall Pro: Online sync from Essentials, Desktop mentioned too. The pricing page lists QuickBooks Online sync on Essentials ($149/mo billed annually, 5 users), not on Basic. Housecall Pro's QuickBooks page says it integrates with both QuickBooks Online and Desktop and that invoices, customers, line items and payments push into QuickBooks automatically; it doesn't say which plan you need for Desktop, so ask before you buy. More: Housecall Pro pricing.
  • ServiceM8: on every plan, with two-way payments. QuickBooks Online, Xero and MYOB are listed on all plans, Free included. ServiceM8's guide says invoices go to QuickBooks Online when you approve them on the Invoicing page, payments recorded in either program sync to the other, and clients and materials stay in sync both ways once they've been linked (changes update within 20 minutes). Invoices created in QuickBooks don't come back to ServiceM8, and staff don't sync. QuickBooks Desktop isn't listed. Paid plans are priced by jobs per month ($29 for 50 jobs up to $349 for 1,500+), not by user; see ServiceM8 vs Jobber.
  • Kickserv: the cheapest two-way sync with Desktop as an option. QuickBooks Online is on every plan, starting with Start ($60/mo billed annually, 5 users). QuickBooks Desktop costs $50/mo extra and needs Run ($119/mo billed annually, 10 users) or Scale. Kickserv calls its integration two-way: invoices, payments, customers and items sync back and forth, your QuickBooks customer and item lists are pulled into Kickserv at setup, and changes made to an invoice in QuickBooks overwrite Kickserv's copy. It recommends logging payments in only one of the two programs. Its QuickBooks page lists Online, Self-Employed, Pro, Premier, Enterprise and QuickBooks for Mac.
  • Service Fusion: Online and Desktop on every plan. All three plans list QuickBooks Integration, and the pricing FAQ says it works with QuickBooks Online and Desktop. Its help center says Online connects directly, while Desktop needs a small Service Fusion plugin installed on the computer that runs QuickBooks, and that plugin is Windows only. Every plan has unlimited users, starting at $220/mo billed annually ($259/mo monthly).
  • Workiz: on every plan, but prices aren't published. The pricing page lists QuickBooks Online sync on Standard, Pro and Ultimate. Workiz's QuickBooks page says it works with Online and Desktop and syncs invoices, Workiz Pay payments, consumer financing transactions, taxes, Workiz Expense Card transactions and customer details, and that you can choose which items sync and when. You have to request pricing for every plan.
  • GorillaDesk: one-way push to QuickBooks Online. QuickBooks Online sync starts on Pro ($99/mo per route, unlimited users). GorillaDesk's help center calls it a one-way push of customers, invoices and payments, with optional tax, discount, Stripe fee and credit syncing to accounts you pick. You can batch-sync invoices from Reports. QuickBooks Desktop isn't supported. More: GorillaDesk pricing.
  • QuoteIQ: from Pro. QuoteIQ's pricing page lists QuickBooks on Pro ($199.99/mo, 4 users; extra users $25/mo each) and up, alongside job costing and text automation. The page names QuickBooks Online; sync direction and Desktop support aren't stated.

The cheapest rows aren't like-for-like: ServiceM8 caps jobs per month rather than users, and GorillaDesk charges per route, so a 5-person crew running 3 trucks pays for 3 routes ($199/mo on Pro). Kickserv's Desktop option adds $50/mo and needs Run. Card processing, QuickBooks itself and add-ons aren't included. For the same math without the QuickBooks requirement, see field service software cost for 1 vs 5 users and the pricing tracker.

One-way vs two-way: what it means day to day

  • One-way (Jobber, GorillaDesk): you create customers, invoices and payments in the field app and they're pushed into QuickBooks. Changes you make in QuickBooks don't come back, so whoever does your books should treat the field app as the master copy. Jobber notes that a paid status recorded in QuickBooks won't show on the Jobber invoice.
  • Two-way (Kickserv, and ServiceM8 for payments and clients): a payment your bookkeeper records in QuickBooks shows up in the field app, which helps if customers mail checks to the office. The trade-off is overwrites: Kickserv says invoice changes made in QuickBooks overwrite Kickserv's copy, and ServiceM8 deletes a payment when it's deleted in QuickBooks.
  • QuickBooks Desktop users have fewer choices: Kickserv (+$50/mo on Run and up) and Service Fusion (Windows plugin) say so on their own pages, and Housecall Pro and Workiz mention Desktop on their QuickBooks pages. Jobber and GorillaDesk say they don't support it.

Trade-specific tools with QuickBooks

If you run one trade, these tools from our trade guides also sync with QuickBooks (from each tool's last verified pricing page):

  • Pool: Pool Brain (QuickBooks Online two-way sync), Pool Office Manager (QuickBooks Online two-way sync as a $25/mo add-on; its page also says it works with Desktop) and Skimmer (QuickBooks Online). See pool service software.
  • Lawn and landscaping: LMN (QuickBooks Online on Starter, Online and Desktop on Professional), Service Autopilot (two-way QuickBooks Online included on Elite, call for pricing on Pro and Pro Plus), Yardbook (QuickBooks sync on Enterprise only) and LawnPro (included on Plus, add-on below). See landscaping business software.
  • Snow: Yeti sends invoicing data to QuickBooks Online; Plowdesk has no live sync, only CSV export. See snow removal software.
  • Pest: GorillaDesk (above) and FieldRoutes (QuickBooks Online listed, package not specified). See pest control software.

Before you connect

Back up your QuickBooks file first, decide which program is the master for customers and payments, and match your invoice numbering so the two don't collide (Service Fusion's Desktop setup guide tells you to start its invoice numbers above your last QuickBooks invoice). Then work through the software buying checklist and ask the vendor to show the sync on a trial account before you move your customer list.

faq: Which field service software works with QuickBooks Desktop?

From the vendor pages checked 2026-11-22: Kickserv (QuickBooks Desktop $50/mo extra on Run and up), Service Fusion (all plans, through a Windows-only plugin), and Housecall Pro and Workiz, whose QuickBooks pages say they support Desktop. Jobber and GorillaDesk say they only sync with QuickBooks Online. ServiceM8 lists QuickBooks Online, Xero and MYOB.

Yes, QuickBooks Online only, starting on the Connect plan ($99/mo billed annually or $139/mo with no commitment for 1 user). Jobber's new integration syncs clients, products and services, invoices, payments and timesheets one way from Jobber to QuickBooks. It doesn't sync with QuickBooks Desktop.
What is the cheapest field service software with QuickBooks integration?

ServiceM8 includes QuickBooks Online sync on every plan, including its Free plan (1 user, 30 jobs a month) and Starter at $29/mo (unlimited users, 50 jobs a month). Kickserv includes QuickBooks Online on Start at $60/mo billed annually ($75/mo monthly) with 5 users.

It depends on the tool. Jobber and GorillaDesk push data one way into QuickBooks. Kickserv says invoices, payments, customers and items sync both ways. ServiceM8 sends invoices to QuickBooks Online, while payments, clients and materials sync both ways.
Does Housecall Pro include QuickBooks on the Basic plan?
No. Housecall Pro's pricing page lists QuickBooks Online sync on Essentials ($149/mo billed annually, $189/mo monthly, 5 users) and MAX, not on Basic.
Is QuickBooks included in the price of these apps?
No. QuickBooks is a separate subscription from Intuit. Housecall Pro's QuickBooks page says so directly, and none of the prices on this page include it.
